## 3. The evidence that moved it

A note that governs every claim below, and every claim in May and June. This
quarter was read against **titles and journals only** — no abstracts were
available for 2023. A title states a direction; it does not state an effect
size, a control, or a population. Where the argument below depends on
something a title cannot carry, it says so instead of asserting it.

**The microbiome arrives at three evidence grades in the same month, from three
independent groups.** [37028428](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028428/)
(*Cell*) names an organism and the dietary tryptophan metabolite it releases as
required for checkpoint inhibitor efficacy.
[37053311](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37053311/) (*Science*) engineers skin
commensals into an antitumour agent — the same biology built as a drug rather
than observed as a correlate. [36914893](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36914893/)
(*Nat Med*) reads the effect in patients receiving CD19 CAR-T, with antibiotic
exposure separated out so the microbial signal survives the obvious confounder.
Mechanism, manufactured agent, and human correlate, in four weeks, in three
journals. That is the strongest structure literature alone can offer, and it is
why `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` takes +4 this month.

**A second convergence, on the antigen space, and it is not confined to this
month.** [36973455](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36973455/) reads
transposable elements pan-cancer as a source of tumour-specific antigens;
[37012458](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37012458/) reaches the same
conclusion from chimeric TE–gene transcripts — same journal, same month,
different groups. The corpus already holds
[36735774](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735774/) (*Sci Immunol*, February)
on noncanonical exon–TE splice junctions as immunogenic neoantigens. Three
groups across two months are enlarging the `neoantigen-vaccines` target space
away from point mutations, which is the part of the thread's claim — that the
space is *large enough* — that mutational burden alone has never settled.

**The neural arm gets an intervention rather than an observation.**
[37099632](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37099632/) (*Sci Transl Med*):
β-blockade changes what an anthracycline does to metastasis. The thread asserts
that neurotransmitters are a shared currency between the neural, microbial and
lymphoid arms; a currency you can spend to alter the outcome of an existing
cytotoxic drug is a materially stronger form of that claim than one you can only
measure. The title does not give the effect size, and this is a mouse result.

**Engineered cell therapy leaves the B cell, at the highest evidence grade the
thread can reach.** [37018492](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37018492/)
(*NEJM*): a GD2-directed CAR-T in relapsed high-risk neuroblastoma — a solid
tumour, in children, against a non-CD19 antigen, in the journal that publishes
registrational readouts. `cell-therapy` is +2/−1 this month and this is the
supporting half.

**Interception acquires two clinical-grade anchors and changes state.**
[36990610](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36990610/) (*Lancet Oncol*) is a
prospective cohort substituting endoscopic surveillance for prophylactic total
gastrectomy in hereditary diffuse gastric cancer — the precursor treated as
something to watch and act on rather than pre-emptively resect.
[37046089](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37046089/) (*Nature*) puts
extrachromosomal DNA amplification inside Barrett's oesophagus, giving the
precursor a molecular event instead of a histological grade. Together they move
`interception` from too-early to forming. Neither reports an intervention
outcome, and the status change is as much a fact about the thread's small card
count as about the month.

**On the meeting in this month.** Section 6 shows 6,360 AACR 2023 abstracts,
because the meeting ran 14–19 April. The journal papers above were published
alongside that meeting, not after it. A journal title cannot evidence a
podium-to-paper interval in either direction — it carries no submission date, no
presentation history, and no way to distinguish a paper that followed a talk from
one that was in press when the talk was given. Nothing in this briefing should be
read as the meeting leading the literature or the literature trailing the meeting,
and no `clinical-practice` card was written for this month for exactly that
reason. Simultaneity has been mistaken for lead in this corpus once already and
it cost a published conclusion.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[37020027](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37020027/) (*Nature*): a blinded,
randomized trial of sonographers versus AI for cardiac function assessment. This
is the strongest clinical result for machine learning in the month, and the model
that produces it is a single-task echocardiography model. `foundation-models`
claims that *scaling* data and parameters is what carries a model into clinical
use; the clinical win here is carried by a narrow model instead, and the thread
moves too-early → contested on it. The trial design is the reason this counts —
blinded and randomized is a grade almost nothing in the AI literature reaches.

[36822206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36822206/) (*Immunity*): RORγ+
regulatory T cells are the emissaries that carry a microbial regeneration signal
to distant tissue. `suppressive-population-inversion` tracks cases where a
population nominated for depletion turns out to be doing necessary work, and this
is one: the cost of removing these cells is tissue repair. The thread's Q1 run —
CD200+ CTLs, IL-5-producing CD4 cells with eosinophils, CD39 marking
tumour-reactive rather than exhausted T cells — continues rather than pauses.

[37072350](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37072350/) (*JITC*): a multicentre
EBMT registry documents severe cytopenia after CD19 CAR-T, read alongside
[37045474](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37045474/) on the endotheliopathy and
hemostatic imbalance underlying CAR-T toxicities. The limiting problem in the
platform's best-established indication is haematological, not antigen choice —
which is a constraint on generalizing the platform, not on choosing targets for it.

### (b) Method credibility

[37130797](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37130797/) (*Genome Res*): STARR-seq
reproducibility is challenged. This matters beyond the assay, because STARR-seq
output is used as ground truth by regulatory-genomics models — an unreliable
assay does not merely produce bad enhancer calls, it produces confidently wrong
benchmarks. Read with [37072822](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37072822/), the
ENCODE Imputation Challenge's critical assessment of cross-cell-type epigenomic
imputation, and [36973549](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36973549/) on the
reliability and accuracy of single-molecule FRET: three audits of established
measurement in one month.

[37097356](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37097356/) (*JAMA*): thirty-two
randomized trials re-run as nonrandomized database emulations, with the agreement
reported as a measured quantity. The observational literature is being tested
against its own gold standard rather than trusted, and the escalation this thread
tracks — from the model, to the pipeline, to the instrument — here reaches the
study design itself.
